stem:
Allyl chloride is an important chemical used in the manufacture of plastics, pharmaceuticals and pesticides.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Give the systematic name of allyl chloride.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
Allyl chloride can be produced by many different methods. The most common method is chlorination of propene which proceeds via a free-radical substitution mechanism.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}
parts.text:
The initiation step in this reaction is the formation of chlorine radicals ($\text{Cl}^{\bullet}$) from $\text{Cl}_2$ molecules.

State the conditions required to initiate this reaction.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The propenyl radical, $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2{}^{\bullet}$, is formed in the first propagation step of the reaction.

Write an equation to show the formation of $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2{}^{\bullet}$ in this propagation step.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why the free-radical substitution reaction gives a low yield of allyl chloride.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
(c)(i)
parts.stem:
A series of reactions starting from allyl chloride is shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_04.png}}
parts.text: Suggest a reagent that can be used in reaction 1.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
In reaction 2, the organic product of reaction 1 is mixed with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and an organic acid, and then heated under reflux.

State the role of the concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. Identify the organic acid used.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: State the name of the mechanism that occurs in reaction 3.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text:
The organic product of reaction 3 is $\mathbf{Y}$.

$\mathbf{Y}$ can be hydrolysed using excess aqueous $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to form $\mathbf{Z}$.

The molecular formula of $\mathbf{Z}$ is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_4$.

Draw the structure of $\mathbf{Z}$.
